chunks: From the father (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying
Quarrelling destroys religion, puts an end to good deeds, and leaves nothing but doubt as its heir.

key_terms.تُحْبِطُ: Nullifies or puts an end to

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of quarrelling according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) warning that persistent quarrelling (al-khusumah) not only erodes faith and nullifies good deeds but also breeds doubt (shakk). This hadith is central to the Shia discourse on avoiding speculative theology (kalam) and contentious debate regarding Allah's essence, emphasizing that excessive argumentation often leads to spiritual uncertainty rather than clarity.
